The root of the word implies a return to balance after an offense, emphasizing that God is a just judge. This reminds believers that God takes sin seriously and that there are consequences to our actions.

34.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, as the Israelites wander in the desert after their liberation from slavery in Egypt, a pivotal moment in their formation as God's people.
34.passage: In Exodus 32, Moses intercedes for the people after they worship the golden calf. God announces here that He will continue to guide His people through His angel, but He will not forget their sins, highlighting the tension between divine grace and justice.
34.culture: In Israelite culture, the idea of an angel as a guide was common, representing God's presence and direction. Sin was perceived not only as a personal offense but also as a rupture of the communal relationship with God.
34.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the duality of God's nature: He is both a loving guide and a just judge. The promise of the angel's presence assures protection, while the warning of punishment reminds us of the seriousness of sin and the necessity of repentance.
34.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God is always present to guide His people, even in moments of disobedience. It reminds us that while we may benefit from His grace, we must also be aware of the consequences of our actions. This invites us to live in accordance with His will and to seek reconciliation with Him through repentance.

mots.sens: This word means 'to strike' or 'to punish'. It evokes the idea of divine punishment in response to disobedience. In this context, it underscores the seriousness of the sin of the people of Israel, who chose to worship an idol instead of remaining faithful to the Lord. It reminds us that God is just and that sin has consequences.

This term translates as 'people' and refers to the nation of Israel as a whole. It reflects the idea of community and collective identity, emphasizing that sin is not only individual but also communal. Spiritually, this reminds us that the actions of a group can have repercussions on the entire faith community.

This word means 'calf' and, in the biblical context, it represents idolatry and deviation from true worship. The golden calf made by Aaron symbolizes the human tendency to create idols from what is material. This highlights the danger of substituting our worship of God with visible and tangible things.

This term means 'God' and is often used to denote divine sovereignty and power. In this verse, it is important to note that the people chose to turn away from the true God to turn towards an image made by human hands. This underscores the necessity of recognizing God's greatness and remaining faithful to Him in our worship.

35.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites were freed from slavery in Egypt and were on their way to the Promised Land under Moses' leadership.
35.passage: Exodus 32 describes the rebellion of the people of Israel against God by making a golden calf while Moses is on Mount Sinai. This chapter illustrates the fragility of human faith in the absence of tangible signs of divine presence.
35.culture: In ancient culture, calves were often associated with deities and worship rituals. This shows how the Israelites, influenced by Egyptian practices, sought physical representations of God, thus betraying their commitment to the Lord.
35.interpretation: This verse reveals God's anger at the idolatry and disobedience of His people. It reminds us that even in a context of grace, sin has consequences and that God does not tolerate unfaithfulness towards Him.
35.commentaire: This passage encourages us to examine our own hearts and to question the 'idols' we may have in our lives. It is essential to remain firmly attached to our faith in God and not to let distractions or external influences lead us away from our commitment to Him. As a community of believers, we must support one another to avoid falling into the temptation of idolatry.
